title: Japanese Army numeric kana cipher, 1902-04: four domestic telegrams in a two-digit coordinate table (JACAR C09122911500, C09123116600, C09122909900, C03020059400)

steps.what: Contributor: JACAR catalogue searches and frame-by-frame viewing of the 1901-02 General Staff telegram files (about 420 items, 1,088 frames) and 235 items of the 1904 Army Ministry Daijiki; C09123116600 found by searching catalogue text for digit runs.
Contributor: digits of five telegrams transcribed by Claude; blind second transcriptions by Codex and Sonnet (lowest 97.2%, 100%, 84.6%, 87.5% for the four read).

Contributor: C09122909900's 12 pairs against the furigana of the outgoing draft (カイグン, エンシウ): n = 10, first digit mod 5 = vowel, >= 5 voiced, columns a9 ka8 sa7 in reverse gojuon order; table completed by the rule.
Contributor: C09122911500 35/35 against its translation (only the ba column fixed from it); C03020059400 10/12; permutation control 0/1000 (max 16 for 0110).
Contributor: C09123116600, no translation, reads ヨヨウノカンコクチズダイヨ (要用ノ韓国地図貸与), fitting the reply draft sending maps of Korea; kana-bigram control 0/1000 permuted tables at or above the reading.
Contributor: C09122806100 (1901) tried with the 1902 table, periodic additives of period 1-7, vowel-digit rules and iroha/gojuon shifts; nothing fits (the same ニ is 91 and 69).

Project: decode.py written from the stated table; the four telegrams decode as claimed (35/35, 11/12, 10/12, ヨヨウノカンコクチズダイヨ); shuffled-digit control, 1,000 tables each: max 16, 6, 6 against 35, 11, 10.

Project: JACAR PDFs fetched; every digit of frames 0110 and 0026 checked against the images. Found the contributor's data/transcription.txt and telegrams.tsv stale for 0110 (34 pairs, missing 18); the image and the form's 72-character count support READING.md's 35 pairs.

validation.notes: Japanese kana plaintext, no Japanese model in lang/; a shuffled-digit permutation control against the filed translations was run instead (decode.py control: max 16, 6, 6 of 1,000 against 35, 11, 10)

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The table was inferred from one telegram's digits against the furigana of its outgoing draft and then completed by its coordinate rule; the filed translations of two more telegrams and a reply draft check it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode_out.txt, unit digit pairs: all 73 pairs of ct_*.txt take a value from the table (80 end mark included).

gaps.detail: The image shows 七; writer's or transmission error; JBIG2 scan.

gaps.item: C03020059400 pairs 5 and 7 (09 for ハ, 88 for ジ)
gaps.detail: One digit off each; the 九/四 doubt needs the original.

outcome.notes: fraction_coherent = 69 of 72 cipher pairs (end mark not counted) agree with the filed translation or give sense. The 35/35 of C09122911500 is partly circular (the table's shape was completed with it in view; one column value came from it); C09123116600 is the independent test but has only 13 pairs and two irregular spellings. AI transcriptions only. Outside the LLM paper's scope (Japanese, not European classical); contributed.

credits.note: Found the numeric kana telegrams in JACAR, reconstructed the 1902-04 table, read four telegrams with controls; Claude Opus 5.5, Codex and Sonnet, no human check
The General Staff's and Army Ministry's filed translations and the furigana of the outgoing draft, used as cribs

prior.where: Contemporary decoded texts filed with three of the four telegrams (they are the cribs). No earlier reconstruction of the table found (contributor's PRIOR_CHECK.md, 20 Oct 2026; Cryptiana's meijiarmy.htm describes 1874 and 1894 Army coordinate ciphers in iroha order).

human: Contributed: Harumi-Matsuba directed the work; Claude Opus 5.5 searched JACAR, transcribed, built the table and ran the controls; Codex and Claude Sonnet made blind second transcriptions. No human checked the transcriptions. The project re-implemented the table, reran the control and checked two forms against the images.
